subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Windmills: Harvesting Invisible Power
description: A micro-lesson that makes Windmills: Harvesting Invisible Power usable.

hook.text: In the 7th century, Persian engineers built the first windmills. They spun horizontally, not vertically.

buildup.text: By the 12th century, Europeans redesigned them with vertical sails to catch wind from any direction.

discovery.text: Windmills could grind grain 10 times faster than a person. They freed thousands from manual labor.

twist.text: The Dutch used windmills to pump water and reclaim land from the sea. Half of the Netherlands exists because of them.

climax.text: At their peak, 10,000 windmills powered the Dutch economy. They were the factories of their age.

quiz.question: What unusual task did Dutch windmills perform beyond grinding grain?
options: They powered looms to weave cloth at high speed
They pumped water to reclaim land from the sea
They generated heat for glassmaking furnaces
